problems.title: Prime-power cancellation
problems.question: Evaluate 12³·27⁴/(4²·9⁷).
problems.idea: Factor or combine the data, retaining all possible roots and geometric positions.
steps: The quotient is 2²3=12.

problems.title: A polynomial remainder
problems.question: Find the remainder when3x²+8x−1 is divided by x+3.
problems.idea: Factor or combine the data, retaining all possible roots and geometric positions.
formulas: The remainder theorem gives P(−3).
steps: It equals 27−24−1=2.

problems.title: Substitute a residue
problems.question: x=11n+2, y=4x−3. Find y’s remainder modulo11.
problems.idea: Factor or combine the data, retaining all possible roots and geometric positions.
steps: The remainder is 5.

problems.title: Supplementary angles and20%
problems.question: One supplementary angle is 20% of the other. Find their difference.
problems.idea: Factor or combine the data, retaining all possible roots and geometric positions.
formulas: Their ratio is 1:5, and their sum 180°.
steps: The angles are 30°,150°, so their difference is 120°.

problems.title: Distances to a tangent and parallel diameter
problems.question: A circle point is 5 from a tangent and 7 from the diameter parallel to it. Find the circle diameter.
problems.idea: Factor or combine the data, retaining all possible roots and geometric positions.
formulas: Put the centre at height 0 and tangent at height R. The point has height±7 and distance R−y=5.
steps: The value y=−7 would give R=−2, impossible. Thus y=7, R=12, and diameter24.

problems.title: A divisor of a power expression
problems.question: Which listed number divides2³·8³−9²?
problems.idea: Factor or combine the data, retaining all possible roots and geometric positions.
formulas: The expression is 4096−81=4015=5·11·73.
steps: Thus 73 divides it; the other listed numbers6,9,27,57,91 do not.

problems.title: Maximum of three completed squares
problems.question: Find the largest value of 31−4x²−y²−9z²+12x−8y+6z.
problems.idea: Factor or combine the data, retaining all possible roots and geometric positions.
formulas: The expression is 57−4(x−3/2)²−(y+4)²−9(z−1/3)².
steps: Every subtracted square is nonnegative. Equality is attained at x=3/2, y=−4, z=1/3.

problems.title: A useful linear combination
problems.question: Given5x+7y=13 and 3x−11y=15, find 2x−y.
problems.idea: Factor or combine the data, retaining all possible roots and geometric positions.
formulas: Add the equations:8x−4y=28.
steps: Divide by 4 to get2x−y=7.

problems.title: Possible arcs with a shared endpoint
problems.question: Arcs AC, AB measure70°,100°. Which listed measure can arc BC have?
problems.idea: Factor or combine the data, retaining all possible roots and geometric positions.
formulas: If B, C lie on the same side of A, the minor arc BC can be 100−70=30°; on opposite sides, it can be 170°.
steps: The corresponding major arcs are 330° and 190°. Among60°,90°,160°,200°,330°, only 330° is possible.
problems.note: If the question intended only the minor arc BC, its possible measures are 30° or 170° and none of the listed numerical choices is correct.

problems.title: Cancel a shared quadratic expression
problems.question: Find a listed possible value of 2x−y if x²−3x+4y=12 and 7y−3x²+9x=21.
problems.idea: Factor or combine the data, retaining all possible roots and geometric positions.
formulas: Add3 times the first equation to the second:19y=57, so y=3.
steps: Then x²−3x=0, so x=0 or 3. The target values are −3 or 3. Only 3 is listed.
problems.answer: 3 among the choices; all possible values are −3 and 3.

problems.title: Parallel line through a reflected point
problems.question: A=(1,−2), B=(4,7). Find the line parallel to AB through B’s reflection in the x-axis.
problems.idea: Factor or combine the data, retaining all possible roots and geometric positions.
formulas: Slope AB=(7+2)/(4−1)=3. The reflected point is(4,−7).
steps: Thus y+7=3(x−4), or y=3x−19.

problems.title: When a linear equation is inconsistent
problems.question: For which a has ax−a=5+2x no root?
problems.idea: Factor or combine the data, retaining all possible roots and geometric positions.
formulas: Rearrange to(a−2)x=a+5.
steps: No root occurs when the coefficient is 0 but the constant is nonzero. At a=2, the equation is 0x=7.

problems.title: Factor a constrained expression
problems.question: Evaluate 2b²+bc−c²−4b+2c if b+c=2.
problems.idea: Factor or combine the data, retaining all possible roots and geometric positions.
formulas: The expression is(2b−c)(b+c−2).
steps: The second factor is 0, so the value is 0.

problems.title: Opposite signs of absolute-value roots
problems.question: For which listed a does|x−17|=a have a negative root product?
problems.idea: Factor or combine the data, retaining all possible roots and geometric positions.
formulas: For a>0, the roots are 17−a,17+a, whose product is 289−a².
steps: It is negative exactly when a>17. Among the choices, only 19 qualifies.

problems.title: An x-intercept of a perpendicular line
problems.question: A line perpendicular to y=−x/5+3 passes through(−5,−5) and meets the x-axis at B=(x, y). Find x+y.
problems.idea: Factor or combine the data, retaining all possible roots and geometric positions.
formulas: The perpendicular slope is 5. Its equation is y+5=5(x+5), or y=5x+20.
steps: At y=0, x=−4, so x+y=−4.

problems.title: A mean as a percentage of another mean
problems.question: 20 women average30 years,30 men average40. What percent of the men’s average is the overall average?
problems.idea: Factor or combine the data, retaining all possible roots and geometric positions.
steps: The desired percentage is 36/40·100%=90%.

problems.title: Combine two ratios
problems.question: a+b+c=142, a:b=3:5, b:c=7:3. Find a−c.
problems.idea: Factor or combine the data, retaining all possible roots and geometric positions.
formulas: Use a:b:c=21:35:15. Their ratio sum is 71, so the scale is 142/71=2.
steps: Thus a=42, c=30, and a−c=12.

problems.title: A prescribed quadratic minimum
problems.question: Find a if ax²−4x+3 has minimum 2.
problems.idea: Factor or combine the data, retaining all possible roots and geometric positions.
formulas: A finite minimum requires a>0. Complete the square:a(x−2/a)²+3−4/a.
steps: Set3−4/a=2 to obtain a=4.

problems.title: A diameter circle in an isosceles triangle
problems.question: ABC has equal sides AB=BC. A semicircle with diameter BC meets base AC at N. Find AN:NC.
problems.idea: Factor or combine the data, retaining all possible roots and geometric positions.
formulas: Thales gives BN⊥AC. In an isosceles triangle, the altitude from the apex also bisects the base.
steps: Therefore AN=NC and the ratio is 1:1.

problems.title: Perpendicular chord lines
problems.question: Extensions of nonintersecting chords AB, CD make30°, and AD is a diameter. Find the angle between AC, BD.
problems.idea: Factor or combine the data, retaining all possible roots and geometric positions.
formulas: Thales gives AC⊥CD and BD⊥AB.
steps: Rotating both lines by 90° preserves their acute angle. Thus angle(AC, BD)=angle(CD, AB)=30°.

problems.title: A parameter in a polynomial degree
problems.question: Find the sum of all m making the degree of 24x¹²y⁷c⁴+18y⁵x¹³z²+32y^|2m−3|c¹²x² equal 27.
problems.idea: Factor or combine the data, retaining all possible roots and geometric positions.
formulas: The first term degrees are 23,20. The last is|2m−3|+14.
steps: Thus|2m−3|=13, giving m=8 or −5. Their sum is 3.

problems.title: Root sum after expansion
problems.question: Find the sum of roots of(2+x)²−1−8x=0.
problems.idea: Factor or combine the data, retaining all possible roots and geometric positions.
formulas: Expand to x²−4x+3=0.
steps: By Vieta, the root sum is 4; indeed the roots are 1,3.

problems.title: Combine a minimum and maximum
problems.question: f(x)=1−x²+4x, g(x)=|f(x)+4|. Find min(g)+max(f).
problems.idea: Factor or combine the data, retaining all possible roots and geometric positions.
formulas: f=5−(x−2)² has maximum 5. The absolute value g is nonnegative and reaches0 when f=−4.
steps: For example x=−1 or 5 gives f=−4. Hence min(g)=0 and the requested sum is 5.

problems.title: All triangles from four allowed lengths
problems.question: How many different triangles can have side lengths chosen from 3,4,7,10, allowing repetition?
problems.idea: Factor or combine the data, retaining all possible roots and geometric positions.
formulas: Count unordered triples with repetition and retain a+b>c for a≤b≤c.
steps: There are 14.

problems.title: Hypotenuse midpoints and altitude feet
problems.question: In acute ABC,∠A=30°, BM, CN are altitudes, E is midpoint AB, F midpoint AC. Find the angle between ME, NF.
problems.idea: Factor or combine the data, retaining all possible roots and geometric positions.
formulas: In right triangle ABM, E is the hypotenuse midpoint, so EA=EM. Thus triangle AEM has equal base angles30°, and line ME makes30° with AC on the opposite side from AB.
steps: In right triangle ACN, F is the hypotenuse midpoint, so FA=FN. Triangle AFN has angle FAN=30°, so AFN=120°; line FN therefore makes60° with AC on the AB side.
The line angle is 30°+60°=90°.
